name: Garter belt

card.summary: A waist-worn suspender garment that holds up stockings with clips, giving a smooth leg line without bands at the thigh and used as a styling piece.

quick.overview:
A garter belt (a suspender belt in British English) is a wide elasticated band worn at or just below the waist with two or three elastic straps on each side. Metal clips attach to the tops of stockings, holding them up without a band squeezing the thigh.

Its looks payoff is styling: a clean, smooth stocking line, a fitted waist look under clothing and a vintage or formal silhouette. It descends from older garters tied below the knee.
quick.how: The belt is worn at or just below the waist so it does not slide down under the pull of the stockings; the clips grip the stocking tops. People wear it with stockings for formal, vintage or costume looks, and with medical support hosiery.
quick.risks: Poor fit can cause pressure marks or slipping. Doctors sometimes suggest stockings with suspenders instead of tights for people prone to yeast or urinary infections [1].

lead: A garter belt, called a suspender belt in the UK, is a wider elasticated strip, usually at least two to three inches wide, with elastic slings on each side ending in metal clips that grip stockings [1]. It evolved from the earlier garter, a band with a hook tied just below the knee [1].

For appearance it gives a smooth stocking line with no thigh band, and is part of vintage-style and formal outfits. Suspenders became a popular alternative to girdles in the 1940s-60s until pantyhose arrived in the early 1960s [1]. Medical use also exists: suspenders hold support hosiery for varicose veins or poor circulation [1].

angle.text: Worn at the waist, the belt keeps stockings taut so the leg line stays smooth, a look people choose for vintage, formal or costume outfits.

paras: The garter is a narrow band that holds up a stocking; the suspender belt is a separate garment with elastic slings and metal clips and adjustable elastic for fit [1]. It sits at or just below the waist so the pull of the stockings does not drag it down [1].

Elizabethan men wore bright garters with hose, and eighteenth-century garters were often embroidered with names or phrases [1]. Before elastic, they used buckles or spiral springs [1]. Suspenders became widely available in the mid-1920s, were issued to British Women's Auxiliary Air Force members in World War II, and were a girdle alternative in the 1940s-60s [1]. Sales rose after the 1988 film Bull Durham, which retailers linked to a black lace garter [1]. Wedding garter traditions continue in the West [1].
No studies found. The term also appears in unrelated surgical literature, such as an acellular dermal matrix 'garter belt' technique for breast implant pockets, which is a different procedure [2].
